tuic: reduce-rtt: quinn needs a TLS session-ticket cache and a pooled connection for 0-RTT; this kernel dials a fresh endpoint per session and rejects the option by name
shadowquic: zero-rtt: JLS 0-RTT needs the pinned authenticated session ticket and a resumption cache
quic-versions: v2: quinn 0.11 implements QUIC v1 only
hysteria: protocol: faketcp loads like the pinned decoder but is refused at dial time: it needs a raw-socket TCP stack, and the pinned non-Linux build is unsupported too
UDP session: the pinned Hysteria v1 datagram session is not implemented, so UDP traffic routed to this family is still dropped and logged

rows: shadowquic/up (controller installed before the handshake because quinn cannot swap a live transport)
hysteria/ports (single-socket destination rewrite; the pinned client opens a new local socket per hop)
approximations_counted_as_residual.reason: rustls cannot emit a uTLS ClientHello, quinn exposes one BBR sender without the pinned profiles/gains, a live quinn transport's congestion factory cannot be replaced after the Brutal negotiation, and the hysteria v1 hop is expressed as destination-port rewriting on one socket. Each is documented and verified for the observable wire path, not claimed as byte-for-byte parity.
